reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses oxidation behavior in HEAs and the role of Al, Cr, Si, but neither mentions yttrium, its segregation, or the reactive element effect in refractory high-entropy alloys. The key premises about Y doping and its specific mechanism are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Yttrium doping (~1 at%) in RHEAs promotes Y segregation at the oxide/metal interface during high-temperature oxidation.
Y segregation enhances adhesion and continuity of an Al2O3-rich oxide scale.
Enhanced scale adhesion and continuity significantly reduces oxygen ingress.
The reactive element effect (REE) mechanism applies to RHEAs with minor Al additions.
A 30% reduction in weight gain and lower spallation are achievable relative to untreated alloy.
